nodes.summary: Let $m \le d + 1$ and let $t_1, \dots, t_m$ be distinct real numbers. Then the points $\gamma(t_1), \dots, \gamma(t_m)$ of the moment curve in $\mathbb{R}^d$ are affinely independent. For $m = d + 1$ this says that no $d + 1$ points of the curve lie on a common affine hyperplane, so the moment curve has order $d$ in the sense of the PCMI notes.
nodes.title: The moment curve has order $d$

nodes.summary: For parameters $t_1, \dots, t_n \in \mathbb{R}$, the cyclic polytope is For distinct parameters and $n > d$ it is a simplicial $d$-polytope; its combinatorial type does not depend on the parameters, as Gale's evenness criterion shows. In Lean the parameters are an arbitrary map $t : \{0, \dots, n - 1\} \to \mathbb{R}$; the theorems add injectivity or strict monotonicity where they need it.
nodes.title: Cyclic polytope

nodes.summary: For parameters $t_1, \dots, t_n \in \mathbb{R}$, the finite set $\{\gamma(t_1), \dots, \gamma(t_n)\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of points on the moment curve. When the parameters are distinct and $d \ge 1$ these are $n$ distinct points. For $d \ge 2$ all of them are vertices of their convex hull, the cyclic polytope, because the parabola $(t, t^2)$ is strictly convex. For $d = 1$ the points lie on a line and only the…
nodes.title: Vertices of a cyclic polytope

nodes.summary: For $d + 1$ distinct parameters, the polytope $C_d(d+1)$ has dimension $d$.
nodes.title: Dimension of a cyclic simplex

nodes.summary: If a continuous linear functional $\ell$ satisfies $\ell(y) = c$ for all $y \in T$, then $\ell(x) = c$ for all $x \in \operatorname{conv} T$, because the hyperplane $\{\ell = c\}$ is convex.
nodes.title: A functional constant on a set is constant on its convex hull

nodes.summary: For every continuous linear functional $\ell$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and every $\tau \in \mathbb{R}$, the polynomial of $\ell$ takes the value $\ell(\gamma(\tau))$ at $\tau$.
nodes.title: Evaluating the polynomial of a functional

nodes.summary: For $d + 1$ distinct parameters, the vertices (extreme points) of $C_d(d+1)$ are exactly the points $\gamma(t_0), \dots, \gamma(t_d)$: each singleton $\{\gamma(t_i)\}$ is a face.
nodes.title: The vertices of a cyclic simplex

nodes.summary: For $d + 1$ distinct parameters, the simplex $C_d(d+1)$ has faces of dimension $k$, for every $k \ge 0$ (in particular $f_d = 1$ and $f_k = 0$ for $k > d$). For $d = 2$ this is a triangle, with f-vector $(f_0, f_1) = (3, 3)$; for $d = 4$ the f-vector is $(5, 10, 10, 5)$, as in the PCMI notes, Lecture 4. These values satisfy the Euler–Poincaré relation and attain the upper bound theorem with $n = d + 1$ vertices.
nodes.title: Face numbers of a cyclic simplex

nodes.summary: For $d + 1$ distinct parameters and a set $T$ of indices, the affine hull of $\operatorname{conv}\{\gamma(t_i) : i \in T\}$ has dimension $|T| - 1$, since these points are affinely independent. In Lean the value for $T = \emptyset$ is $0$ (natural-number subtraction), matching the convention that the direction of the empty affine subspace is the zero space.
nodes.title: Dimension of a face of a cyclic simplex

nodes.summary: For a continuous linear functional $\ell$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, the polynomial where $e_j$ is the $j$-th standard basis vector. It has degree at most $d$, no constant term, and its value at $\tau$ is $\ell(\gamma(\tau))$.
nodes.title: The polynomial of a functional

nodes.summary: A set $S \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ satisfies Gale's evenness condition if for any two indices $j < k$ not in $S$, the number of elements $i \in S$ with $j < i < k$ is even. For example, with $n = 4$ the sets $\{0, 1\}$, $\{1, 2\}$, $\{2, 3\}$ and $\{0, 3\}$ satisfy it and $\{0, 2\}$, $\{1, 3\}$ do not: these are the edges and the diagonals of a convex quadrilateral.
nodes.title: Gale's evenness condition

nodes.summary: Let $t_1 < t_2 < \cdots < t_n$ be real numbers and let $S$ be a set of $d$ indices. Then the points $\gamma(t_i)$, $i \in S$, span a face of the cyclic polytope $C_d(n) = \operatorname{conv}\{\gamma(t_1), \dots, \gamma(t_n)\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, that is, $\operatorname{conv}\{\gamma(t_i) : i \in S\}$ is a face of $C_d(n)$, if and only if $S$ satisfies Gale's evenness condition. Since $d$ points of the moment…
nodes.title: Gale's evenness criterion

nodes.summary: Let $t_1, \dots, t_n$ be distinct real numbers and let $T$ be a set of indices with $2|T| \le d$. Then $\operatorname{conv}\{\gamma(t_i) : i \in T\}$ is a face of the cyclic polytope $C_d(n) \subset \mathbb{R}^d$. In particular every set of at most $\lfloor d/2 \rfloor$ vertices of $C_d(n)$ spans a face: $C_d(n)$ is $\lfloor d/2 \rfloor$-neighborly. Since such vertex sets are affinely independent, it follows that…
nodes.title: Cyclic polytopes are neighborly

nodes.summary: Let $t_0, \dots, t_d$ be $d + 1$ distinct real numbers, so that $C_d(d+1) = \operatorname{conv}\{\gamma(t_0), \dots, \gamma(t_d)\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is a $d$-simplex. For every set $T$ of indices, $\operatorname{conv}\{\gamma(t_i) : i \in T\}$ is a face of $C_d(d+1)$, and it contains $\gamma(t_j)$ only for $j \in T$.
nodes.title: Every vertex set of a cyclic simplex spans a face

nodes.summary: For $d + 1$ distinct parameters, every facet of $C_d(d+1)$ (a face of dimension $d - 1$) contains exactly $d$ of its vertices, so $C_d(d+1)$ is simplicial in the sense of the simplicial-polytope definition. This checks the definition on a concrete polytope.
nodes.title: A cyclic simplex is simplicial

nodes.summary: For $d + 1$ distinct parameters, the faces of the simplex $C_d(d+1)$ are exactly the sets $\operatorname{conv}\{\gamma(t_i) : i \in T\}$ for $T \subseteq \{0, \dots, d\}$, including the empty face ($T = \emptyset$) and the simplex itself ($T$ = all indices). Distinct $T$ give distinct faces, so the face lattice of a $d$-simplex is the Boolean lattice of subsets of its $d + 1$ vertices.
nodes.title: The faces of a cyclic simplex

nodes.summary: The $i$-th coordinate of $\gamma(t) \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is $t^{i+1}$, for $0 \le i < d$ (coordinates are indexed from $0$).
nodes.title: Coordinates of the moment curve

nodes.summary: For $d \ge 1$, distinct parameters give distinct points of the moment curve $\gamma(t) = (t, t^2, \dots, t^d)$: the first coordinate is $t$ itself. For $d = 0$ the curve is the constant map to the single point of $\mathbb{R}^0$.
nodes.title: The moment curve is injective in positive dimension

nodes.summary: For $d \ge 0$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$, the moment curve in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is A curve in $\mathbb{R}^d$ has order (degree) $d$ when no $d + 1$ of its points lie on a common affine hyperplane; the moment curve is the standard example, and cyclic polytopes are convex hulls of finitely many of its points.
nodes.title: The moment curve

nodes.summary: The polynomial of a linear functional on $\mathbb{R}^d$ has degree at most $d$.
nodes.title: Degree of the polynomial of a functional

nodes.summary: Let $t_i$, $i \in S$, be real numbers and let $\tau$ differ from all of them. Then that is, the product has the sign $(-1)^m$: exactly the $m$ factors with $t_i > \tau$ are negative.
nodes.title: Sign of a product of linear factors

nodes.summary: If $p$ has degree at most $d$, then $\ell_p(\gamma(\tau)) = p(\tau) - p(0)$ for every $\tau \in \mathbb{R}$. So every polynomial of degree at most $d$ is, up to a constant, a linear functional restricted to the moment curve.
nodes.title: A polynomial of degree at most $d$ along the moment curve

nodes.summary: For a real polynomial $p = \sum_k p_k X^k$ and $d \ge 0$, the linear functional on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (coordinates indexed from $0$). Along the moment curve it evaluates $p$ up to its constant term.
nodes.title: The functional of a polynomial

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
